text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak meets Sudanese opposition leader Sadeq al-Mahdi.

- President Mubarak will hold an expanded ministerial meeting tomorrow morning on final details of the project to develop the south of the valley, before he visits the Toshka area to give the starting signal for the Project of the Century.

- Local Government Minister Mahmoud Sherif said that investment offices in the provinces have received 4,901 project applications so far for investments with a total value of 48.5 billion pounds ($14.3 billion), apart from tourism projects.

- The cabinet will discuss in its next meeting a programme to privatise water stations and sewerage systems in the new towns and provinces. The programme will for the first time allow the private sector to set up and manage water and sewerage services at prices fixed and approved by the government.

- It has been decided to increase cement production this year to 19 million tonnes, one million tonnes more than last year. A further two million tonnes will be imported to cover the demands of domestic consumption. The chairman of the Holding Company for Mining and Refractories said there was no move towards raising cement prices in the coming period.

- Port Said court of first instance ordered the British company International Shipping to pay 300 million pounds in compensation for the damage one of its Panamanian-registered vessels did to coral reefs in the Red Sea on September 11, 1989.
- In an interview with the "Good Morning Egypt" programme, President Mubarak said the Palestinian problem must be solved this year.

- Finance Minister Mohyeddin el-Gharib said parliament will discuss within days a draft amendment eliminating the word "confiscation" from the current customs law. Instead of confiscating goods imported improperly, the authorities will instead impose a fine.

- The chairman of the board of state-owned company Egyptian Petrochemicals (EPC), Ashri Mohamed Ashri, was shot dead by his son, a 22-year-old police officer who thought his father had taken a second wife.
- It has been decided to increase the amount of chicken, meat and fish supplied to consumer cooperatives for the start of the fasting month of Ramadan.
- The funeral took place yesterday of Hafez Ismail, former national security adviser to the president, who died on Wednesday at the age of 77.

- Abdelwahhab el-Habbak, former chairman of the state's Holding Company for Engineering Industries, was remanded in custody for a further 45 days for questioning about 200 million pounds he allegedly acquired through his post.
